## Dossier: Clinical Notes (Note Threads / Messages) — Backend

### FHIR mapping
**None found.** No import, comment, or reference to FHIR (`Communication`, `DocumentReference`, `ClinicalImpression`, or any `build.fhir.org` link) exists anywhere in [notes.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/models/notes.py), [notes.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py), [notes_spec.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/notes_spec.py), or [thread_spec.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/thread_spec.py). This is a plain internal messaging/audit-note feature with no claimed FHIR resource alignment in code. (Verified via targeted grep for `fhir|Communication|DocumentReference|ClinicalImpression` in `care/emr/models/notes.py` — zero matches, and no such terms in the viewset/spec files either.)

### Key attributes

**`NoteThread`** — `care/emr/models/notes.py:6-11`

| Field | Type | Required (create)? | Nullable/default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `CharField(max_length=255)` | Yes on model spec but **required in `NoteThreadSpec`** (`title: str = Field(..., max_length=255)`, [thread_spec.py:12-13](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/thread_spec.py#L12-L13)) | model allows `null=True, blank=True` but pydantic spec makes it mandatory (`...`) — model-level nullability is effectively unreachable via the API | Thread label |
| `patient` | FK to `emr.Patient`, `CASCADE` | set server-side from URL, not user-supplied (`__exclude__ = ["patient", "encounter"]`, thread_spec.py:10) | not null | Set in `perform_create` (notes.py viewset:82) |
| `encounter` | FK to `emr.Encounter`, `CASCADE` | Optional | `null=True, blank=True` | Only settable on **create**, via `NoteThreadCreateSpec.encounter: UUID4 \| None` with a `field_validator` checking existence (thread_spec.py:16-23). **Not present in `NoteThreadUpdateSpec`** — encounter cannot be changed/removed on update (thread_spec.py:32-33, empty subclass) |

**`NoteMessage`** — `care/emr/models/notes.py:14-17`

| Field | Type | Required? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thread` | FK to `NoteThread`, `CASCADE` | server-set | excluded from spec (`__exclude__ = ["thread"]`, notes_spec.py:11), set in `perform_create` from URL path |
| `message` | `TextField` | Yes (`message: str`, no default) | notes_spec.py:14 |
| `message_history` | `JSONField(default=dict)` | n/a (read-only, server-managed) | See semantics below |
| `encounter` | **not on model** — set dynamically as an attribute in `perform_create` only if request body has `encounter` (viewset notes.py:127-131) | optional | **This is a bug/ambiguity — see SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES #4** |

**`message_history` semantics** ([notes_spec.py:20-35](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/notes_spec.py#L20-L35)):
On every update, `NoteMessageUpdateSpec.perform_extra_deserialization` fetches the **pre-update** DB object (`old_obj = NoteMessage.objects.get(external_id=obj.external_id)`) and appends a snapshot of the *old* message to `obj.message_history["history"]` (a list) before the new message overwrites `obj.message`. Each history entry is a dict: `{"message": <old message text>, "created_by": {"username", "external_id"}, "edited_at": <now>, "created_at": <old modified_date>}`. Note the field names are misleading: `created_by`/`created_at` in a history entry actually refer to the **editor and the time of the previous version**, not the original author — `old_obj.created_by` is the message's original author (fixed per message) while `old_obj.modified_date` is when that prior version was last saved. This is only invoked on **update**, never on create, so `message_history` starts as `{}` for a new message and is only populated after ≥1 edit.

**Audit fields from `EMRBaseModel`** (`care/emr/models/base.py:8-27`, applies to both models):
- `history` (JSONField, default `{}`) — inherited but **unused** for notes; a `# TODO Handle historical data...` in `EMRUpdateMixin.perform_update` (`care/emr/api/viewsets/base.py:177`) confirms this generic history mechanism isn't implemented — notes instead built their own bespoke `message_history` field.
- `meta` (JSONField, default `{}`) — inherited, unused for notes.
- `created_by` / `updated_by` — FK to `users.User`, `SET_NULL`, nullable. Set automatically: `created_by`/`updated_by` on create (`EMRCreateMixin.perform_create`, base.py:97-98), `updated_by` on update (`EMRUpdateMixin.perform_update`, base.py:178). Serialized as `dict` via `cls.serialize_audit_users(mapping, obj)` in both read specs (notes_spec.py:49, thread_spec.py:37).
- Plus, from `BaseModel` (`care/utils/models/base.py:14-24`): `external_id` (UUID4, unique), `created_date`/`modified_date` (auto timestamps), `deleted` (soft-delete boolean, default `False`).

**None.** Neither `NoteThread` nor `NoteMessage` nor their resource specs define any `Choices`/enum class — confirmed by reading the full contents of [notes.py (model)](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/models/notes.py), [notes_spec.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/notes_spec.py), and [thread_spec.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/thread_spec.py) — no status field, no type field, no coded value of any kind exists on threads or messages.

### Behavioral rules and validations

1. **Thread creation — patient/encounter mismatch check** ([notes.py:80-84](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L80-L84)): `perform_create` sets `instance.patient` from the URL, then if `instance.encounter and instance.encounter.patient != instance.patient`, raises `ValidationError("Patient Mismatch")`. Verified by `test_create_thread_on_encounter_with_patient_mismatch` (test_notes_api.py).
2. **Message creation — thread-must-belong-to-patient check** ([notes.py:112-118](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L112-L118)): `get_thread_obj()` raises `ValidationError("Thread does not belong to the patient")` if `thread.patient_id != patient.id`. Verified by `test_list_notes_with_patient_thread_mismatch`, `test_get_note_details_with_patient_thread_mismatch`.
3. **Message creation — optional per-message encounter override with patient mismatch check** ([notes.py:120-127](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L120-L127)): if the create request body has an `encounter` key, it's resolved and if `encounter.patient != instance.thread.patient`, raises `ValidationError("Patient Mismatch")`. Otherwise `instance.encounter = encounter` (attribute set on an in-memory model instance — see issue below, since `NoteMessage` has no `encounter` DB field).
4. **Message retrieve/update — message-belongs-to-thread check**: `authorize_retrieve` ([notes.py:154-157](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L154-L157)) and `authorize_update` ([notes.py:145-150](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L145-L150)) both raise `ValidationError("Message does not belong to the thread")` if `model_instance.thread != thread` (thread resolved from URL). Verified by `test_get_note_details_with_invalid_thread`.
5. **"Cannot update message created by another user"** ([notes.py:145-146](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L145-L146)): `authorize_update` raises `PermissionDenied("Cannot Update Message Created by Other User")` if `self.request.user.id != model_instance.created_by_id` — this check applies **regardless of role/permission**, i.e., even a facility admin cannot edit someone else's message. No corresponding test exercises this exact message in `test_notes_api.py`, but the code path is unconditional (see AMBIGUITIES).
6. **Threads can be renamed**: `NoteThreadUpdateSpec` only inherits `title` (thread_spec.py:32-33) — `encounter` is excluded from update, so only `title` is updatable via `PUT`/`PATCH` on a thread. Verified by `test_update_thread`.
7. **Deletion**: **Not possible for either threads or messages.** Neither `NoteThreadViewSet` nor `NoteMessageViewSet` includes `EMRDestroyMixin` (only `EMRCreateMixin, EMRRetrieveMixin, EMRUpdateMixin, EMRListMixin` are mixed in, notes.py:31-45, 108-112) — there is no `destroy` action wired, so DELETE is not exposed on these routes.
8. **Ordering**:
   - Threads: `.order_by("-created_date")` (newest thread first) — `NoteThreadViewSet.get_queryset` (notes.py:106).
   - Messages: on `list` action, `.filter(thread=thread).order_by("-created_date")` (newest message first); on other actions (retrieve/update), `.order_by("-modified_date")` (notes.py:174-179).
9. **Filtering** (`NoteThreadFilters`, notes.py:26-28): `encounter` — `UUIDFilter` on `encounter__external_id`; `encounter_isnull` — custom `NullFilter` (`care/utils/filters/null_filter.py`) that filters `encounter__isnull=<bool>` when a boolean value is passed, no-op if `None`/absent. `NoteMessageViewSet` has **no `filterset_class`** — the only "filtering" for messages is the implicit `thread` scoping in `get_queryset`.
10. **Global visibility gate (both viewsets' `get_queryset`)**: if the user lacks `can_view_clinical_data` on the patient, the code falls back to checking a `?encounter=` query param — if present, requires `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` on that encounter, else raises `PermissionDenied("Permission denied to user")`. If no `?encounter=` param is present and patient-level view is denied, always `PermissionDenied` (notes.py:93-103, 163-171) — this **query param gate does not verify the referenced encounter is actually linked to any of the returned threads/messages**, it's purely a view-authorization side-channel (see SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES #3).
11. **Encounter completion blocks new clinical writes**: `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` (`care/security/authorization/encounter.py:97-105`) returns `False` if `encounter.status in COMPLETED_CHOICES`, which blocks creating threads/messages tied to a completed encounter — verified by `test_create_note_after_encounter_complete` in test_notes_api.py, which asserts 403 for a completed encounter's thread even without an explicit `encounter` field in the message payload (the thread's own `encounter` gates via `authorize_thread_write`).

### Permissions

| Operation | Scope | Auth check called | Permission slug | Human-readable name | Roles holding it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| List threads | patient-only view | `can_view_clinical_data` (patient.py authz:94) | `can_view_clinical_data` | "Can view clinical data about patients" | `STAFF_ROLE, DOCTOR_ROLE, NURSE_ROLE, ADMIN_ROLE, FACILITY_ADMIN_ROLE` (permissions/patient.py:58-64) |
| List threads | `?encounter=` fallback | `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` (authorization/encounter.py:50-61) | `can_read_encounter_clinical_data` | "Can Read encounter related clinical data" | `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES` = `ADMIN_ROLE, DOCTOR_ROLE, NURSE_ROLE, FACILITY_ADMIN_ROLE` (permissions/encounter.py:14-19, 63-68) |
| Create thread | encounter-scoped | `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` (authorization/encounter.py:97) | `can_write_encounter_clinical_data` | "Update Encounter related clinical data" | `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES` |
| Create thread | patient-only | `can_write_patient_obj` (authorization/patient.py:58) | `can_write_patient` | "Can Update a Patient's data" | `STAFF_ROLE, DOCTOR_ROLE, NURSE_ROLE, ADMINISTRATOR, ADMIN_ROLE, FACILITY_ADMIN_ROLE` (permissions/patient.py:29-38) |
| Update thread | encounter-scoped | `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` | `can_write_encounter_clinical_data` | "Update Encounter related clinical data" | `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES` |
| Update thread | patient-only | `can_write_patient_obj` | `can_write_patient` | "Can Update a Patient's data" | (as above) |
| List messages | patient-only view | `can_view_clinical_data` | `can_view_clinical_data` | "Can view clinical data about patients" | (as above) |
| List messages | `?encounter=` fallback | `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` | `can_read_encounter_clinical_data` | "Can Read encounter related clinical data" | `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES` |
| Create message | thread has encounter | `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` (via `authorize_thread_write`, notes.py:139-150) | `can_write_encounter_clinical_data` | "Update Encounter related clinical data" | `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES` |
| Create message | thread has no encounter | `can_write_patient_obj` (via `authorize_thread_write`) | `can_write_patient` | "Can Update a Patient's data" | (as above) |
| Update message | (in addition to thread-write check) | own-authorship check `self.request.user.id != model_instance.created_by_id` — **no permission slug**, hardcoded rule | n/a | n/a | n/a — applies to any authenticated user regardless of role |
| Update message | thread has encounter | `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` | `can_write_encounter_clinical_data` | "Update Encounter related clinical data" | `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES` |

`super().is_superuser` always bypasses these checks in `PatientAccess`/no explicit superuser bypass exists in `EncounterAccess.can_update_encounter_clinical_data`/`can_view_encounter_clinical_data` methods shown — only `PatientAccess` methods (`can_write_patient_obj`, `can_view_clinical_data`) have an explicit `if user.is_superuser: return True` (authorization/patient.py:58-59, 94-95). `check_permission_in_facility_organization`/`check_permission_in_encounter` (used by `EncounterAccess`) were not traced to a superuser bypass in the excerpts read — flagged under AMBIGUITIES.

### Flows (API-level)

1. **List threads for a patient**: `GET /api/v1/patient/{patient_external_id}/thread/` — optionally `?encounter={uuid}` and/or `?encounter_isnull=true|false`. Requires `can_view_clinical_data` on patient, or (if filtering by `?encounter=`) `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` on that encounter.
2. **Create a patient-level thread** (no encounter): `POST .../thread/` with `{"title": "..."}`. Requires `can_write_patient_obj`.
3. **Create an encounter-scoped thread**: `POST .../thread/` with `{"title": "...", "encounter": "<uuid>"}`. Requires `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` on that encounter; encounter must belong to the same patient or 400 "Patient Mismatch"; encounter must exist or pydantic validator raises "Encounter not found".
4. **Retrieve a thread**: `GET .../thread/{external_id}/` — **no thread-specific authorization is enforced** beyond DRF's default `get_object` (see SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES #1).

This is dead/misleading code — it silently discards user-submitted "encounter" data on a message with no persistence and no serialization, other than being used transiently for the "Patient Mismatch" validation check.
5. **Inconsistent superuser bypass**: `PatientAccess.can_write_patient_obj` / `can_view_clinical_data` explicitly bypass for `user.is_superuser`, but the `EncounterAccess` methods used in the encounter-scoped code paths (`can_update_encounter_clinical_data`, `can_view_encounter_clinical_data`) shown do not have an explicit superuser short-circuit in the excerpts read (they call `check_permission_in_facility_organization`, whose superuser handling was not verified — see AMBIGUITIES). 2. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx#L6-L12), `PatientNotesTab` renders:
   ```tsx
   <NoteManager
     canAccess={true}
     canWrite={true}
     patientId={props.patientData.id}
     encounterId={undefined}
     hideEncounterNotes={true}
   />
   ```

- `get_queryset` requires `can_view_clinical_data` ("Can view clinical data about patients") on the patient.

- read/visibility → gated on `can_view_clinical_data` permission (`PERMISSION_VIEW_CLINICAL_DATA` / `canViewClinicalData` in `src/common/Permissions.tsx`)
- write → gated on `can_write_patient` permission (`PERMISSION_WRITE_PATIENT` / `canWritePatient` in `src/common/Permissions.tsx`)
